model: Claude (written in Claude Code from profiles.json, same rules as scripts/coach_report.py)
headline: High-volume pressure fighter whose attacks aren't converting: 33 strikes/min, 60% initiative, 0 points
summary: CRO does most of the fighting: 2.6x her opponent's strike rate, double the tempo, and she starts 60% of exchanges. None of it has scored (0-4). The data points to conversion and entry timing, not effort: she initiates a lot, but FRA takes the decisive exchanges.
strengths: Work rate: 33.4 strikes/min and 7.7 actions per 10 s, about 2x FRA on both. She keeps the opponent busy.
Initiative: starts 60% of exchanges overall and 71% in clip 02. She sets the rhythm of the bout.
Range control in clip 02 (59%): she presses and pushes FRA back for long stretches.
weaknesses: Conversion: high volume and 0 points. Many attacks are likely being blocked, out of range, or not finished with control.
Simultaneous exchanges go against her: in the exchange that produced FRA's yuko (clip 02, 18.8 s) both threw at the same moment and FRA scored. Her entries leave her open to the counter.
Loses distance after conceding: in clip 03 she controlled range only 31% of the time, so FRA walked her back right after the ippon.
focus: Quality over quantity: fewer, better set-up attacks. A feint or a rhythm change before committing, instead of straight repeated entries.
Entry defense: cover or angle out on the way in, so a simultaneous counter cannot score first.
Reset after conceding: regain the center and the initiative within the first few seconds instead of retreating.
drills: Set-up then attack: 6 x 1 min. Every scoring attempt must come after a feint, a stance switch or a rhythm break; plain straight entries don't count.
Counter-aware entries: 5 x 1 min. The partner counters gyaku-zuki on every entry. CRO must angle off or cover and still finish the technique.
Score-down restart: short rounds that start at 0-3. CRO's only goal in the first 5 s is to take the center back.
caveats: Cohort is just 2 athletes (one bout, split into 3 clips), so percentiles and the gap are illustrative only.
Strike counts come from pose estimation on 360p video and are not yet checked against a human count. CRO's very high rate in clip 01 may include some guard and hand-fighting motion.
standing_pct / gap use bout points share as a placeholder definition.
